_doc: Resource budget per plugin instance (the roadmap's budget table). Read by tests/budget.sh and tests/run_tests.sh.
_skin_mb: sum of w x h x 4 over every skin image, all tabs. Raised from 8 on 2026-10-14 for the five-tab design (23.7 MB on this gauge); the VST-9 probe measured about 2-3 MB of MPC RSS for it on the Force (MPC draws the visible page only). Revisit if performance suffers. 2026-10-14, 0.10 (owner's standing rule): 32 -> 48. The gauge charges every when= mode image of every tab (about 2.2 MB each); CHORDS + BASS with three modes each read 36.4 MB, MELODY's modes will add about 7. The VST-9 probe measured +0.8 MB of MPC RSS for a moded tab while shown (MPC decodes the visible page only). 2026-10-14, 0.12 (owner approved after seeing the numbers): 48 -> 50. The two CHORDS FIX slot layouts (4 large / 8) add a 0.72 MB mode image each; gauge 48.5 MB. 2026-10-16, 0.16 (owner approved after seeing the numbers): 50 -> 52. BASS and MELODY FIX by bar (bar strip, NEW BAR / RESET BAR) make their FIX mode images taller (about 0.5 MB each); gauge 51.0 MB. MPC decodes the visible page only (VST-9 probe). 2026-10-17, 0.17 (owner approved after seeing the numbers): 52 -> 56. The CHORDS page (VST-15): the picker, PROGRESSIONS, VOICING and RHYTHM views each a full centre-panel mode image (~1.6 MB each), the strip / left panel / KEYS hideable on FIX (1.4 MB), drift frames 0.64 MB; IDEAS/SHAPE removed (-0.9 MB); gauge 55.6 MB. MPC decodes the visible page only (VST-9 probe). 2026-10-18, 0.18 (owner approved after seeing the numbers and screenshots): 56 -> 62. The RHYTHM page: the editor/not-editing view shared as one image with small per-view blocks (rview), the RHYTHMS browser and COPY TO… each a full-width view (~2 MB each), knobs shared; gauge 61.1 MB. MPC decodes the visible page only (VST-9 probe). 2026-10-19, 0.19 (owner approved after seeing the numbers): 62 -> 71. The BASS tab (VST-26) replaces IDEAS/SHAPE/FIX A NOTE (-4.9 MB) with the BASS page, its bar editor and STYLE browser, and the BASS RHYTHM page with its RHYTHMS browser and COPY TO… (each a full centre-panel or full-width view, ~1.6-3.7 MB); gauge 70.9 MB. MPC decodes the visible page only (VST-9 probe). 2026-10-20, 0.20: 71 -> 73, owner approved raise for 0.20 MELODY (2026-10-20); measured 72.6 MB. The MELODY JAM and PHRASE pages (VST-27) replace RECIPE/IDEAS/SHAPE/FIX NOTE: JAM 2.4 MB, PHRASE 2.1, its picker 2.0, its bar editor with the strip 2.5, the strip on PHRASE and the picker 0.8, the dot filmstrips 0.3 (the decoded meter strips). 2026-10-22, 0.22: 73 -> 80, owner approved raise after seeing the numbers; measured 78.8 MB. The CHORDS and BASS JAM pages (VST-29): each JAM page 2.44 MB as a full-panel mode image like MELODY's, the BASS strip modes +0.48, the meter strips 0.43, the SWITCH AT cards 0.26.

_cpu: p99 5 -> 7 and worst block 10 -> 13 on 2026-10-14 (owner) for 0.7: the wrapper polls the 0.7 skin's 64 px list cells every 10 ms (about 0.03 points of p99 per cell); the worst block is the bench's synthetic sweep of four random parameters per block (GEN, NEW IDEA). 0.7 measured p99 5.9, worst 11.2. Revisit if performance suffers. 2026-10-14, 0.9 (plan decision 12, owner's standing rule): p99 7 -> 11, worst 13 -> 15. 0.9 measured idle/voices p99 5.0 (was 4.4) but q-link sweep p99 9.1, worst 13.8: the sweep fires four random params per block, now including the CHORDS taps (try an idea, a move, REROLL) that revoice, regenerate lanes and rebuild label caches under the wrapper lock. No user taps that fast. 2026-10-14, 0.10 (owner's standing rule; flagged for review): p99 11 -> 25, worst 15 -> 42. 0.10 measured idle/voices p99 7.5 (polling 254 string cells) and q-link sweep p99 23.4, worst 39.8 (toolchain verdict WARN): the sweep stacks four random taps per block. Per tap on the Force (probe/setcost.c, vst/setcost.txt): worst single setter 335 us (Key, 11.5% of a block); 0.9's worst was 150 us. Chord edits now also rebuild the Bass idea labels. Follow-up: cheaper label rebuilds. 2026-10-14, 0.11 (owner chose 'ship and accept' after reviewing the trend): p99 25 -> 31, worst 42 -> 47. 0.11 measured idle p99 11.2 (the wrapper polls ~350 string cells every 10 ms on the audio thread), q-link sweep 29.9 / 45.6 (WARN); worst single tap 474 us (16% of a block, vst/setcost.txt). 2026-10-15, 0.13 (owner approved after seeing the numbers): p99 31 -> 34, worst 47 -> 51. Idle p99 11.9 (unchanged); q-link sweep 32.8 / 49.3: the sweep now includes the stepped knobs (k_*), each of which regenerates its lane. Worst single tap 528 us (18.2%, vst/setcost.txt). 2026-10-16, 0.14 (owner approved after seeing the numbers): worst 51 -> 75. Idle p99 unchanged; q-link sweep 33-34 / 69-71 over three runs: every chord edit rebuilds labels for up to 64 slots plus the FIX bar strip. Worst single tap 811 us (New Progression, 27.9%, vst/setcost.txt). Follow-up: strip labels only while FIX is shown; skip per-slot work for a loop that repeats its phrase. 2026-10-17, 0.17 (owner approved after seeing the numbers): p99 34 -> 36. Idle p99 15.2 -> 19.1 and q-link sweep p99 34.7 / 35.3 over two runs, worst block 63.0: the CHORDS page (VST-15) adds about 110 polled string cells (60 KEYS). Follow-up: stop _on polling for cells that never light; cache lit states. 2026-10-18, 0.18 (owner approved after seeing the numbers): p99 36 -> 40. 0.18 first measured q-link sweep 74.3 / 127.9 (FAIL): every set ~2x 0.17; fixed (offset table, hashed parse_key, snprintf-free names, colour_cx rank skip): idle p99 22.6 -> 15.3 (0.17: 19.1), no-op tap mean 658 -> 263 us (0.17: 335), worst setter 694 us (vst/setcost.txt); sweep 38.6 / 61.8. The sweep's random param path got heavier with 99 new params: on that path 0.17.1 itself reads 43.1 / 73.6; on 0.17.1's own path this build reads 31.7 / 48.2. 2026-10-22, 0.22 (owner approved after seeing the numbers): p99 40 -> 44, worst 75 -> 80. The q-link sweep read 41.8 / 77.1 and 41.5 / 77.3 over two runs (idle p99 25.4): the sweep's random four-params-a-block path now spans 152 more params (the CHORDS and BASS JAM pages). Real JAM actions on the Force (probe/setcost_jam.c, vst/setcost.txt): block tap ~105 us, knob 1 ~115, TIME up to 266, the audio block at a switch no cost above noise; worst existing setter (Fix Chord) 692 -> 1000 us. Follow-up lever: the +72 polled JAM list cells. 2026-10-24, 0.24 (owner approved after seeing the numbers): p99 44 -> 46. The q-link sweep read 45.2 / 65.3 (45.5 / 64.7, 45.1 / 64.4 over three runs; idle p99 22.2, 0.23: 26.1; worst block 0.23: 76.7): the sweep's random four-params-a-block path now spans ~510 more params (the CHORDS and BASS PHRASE pages). Real PHRASE actions on the Force (probe/setcost_phr.c, vst/setcost.txt): a pick, COPY TO ALL, COPY TO... GO, RESET BAR, LOCK WITH and ANTICIPATE taps (with a follower lane), knobs 5-7 with a JAM block queued all at most 337 us (11.6% of a block); ANTICIPATE adds nothing measurable to the audio block. 2026-10-24, 0.24 release fix (owner approved after seeing the numbers, his option 1): p99 46 -> 49. The device test found PHRASE editor cells (DONE, CANCEL, LOCK) acting on the first touch only: the wrapper's list-tile echo guard dropped MPC's repeated 1 on unpolled never-lit tiles. Fixed in the toolchain (local commit 9e8b0ab, ECHO_GUARD_POLLED_ONLY 1 in vst/vst.json): the guard skips unpolled tiles. The q-link sweep now reads 48.1 / 48.2 / 47.9 (worst block 65.3, idle p99 unchanged at about 23) because the bench's random sets on the ~770 unpolled tap cells all reach the engine as real actions; the same-day pre-fix build read 45.9.

MELODY FIX by bar while playing (FOLLOW off) reads 22.3% of MPC's main thread against the 11.7% closed baseline (10.6 points; vst/ui_cost.json). Offline screen updates are unchanged from 0.13 (20.4/s at 120 BPM), so it is MPC drawing the larger page; 0.14's 2.5 points were CHORDS FIX. 2026-10-17, 0.17 (owner approved after seeing the numbers): 11 -> 30. The CHORDS page (VST-15) with FOLLOW on reads 49.1% against 20.2% closed (the CLIP view, measured the same day; 0.7's 11.7% baseline was stale), +28.9 points; FOLLOW off 35.0%; stopped, nothing. Every UpdateDisplay rebuilds the shown page, and PLAY's pos readout and ph_ playhead change at every 16th on any tab. Follow-up issue: step them per beat. 2026-10-18, 0.18 (owner approved; revisit if performance suffers): 30 -> 35. The RHYTHM view with FOLLOW on reads 53.4% against 19.9% closed (CLIP view, same day), +33.5 points (0.17 CHORDS page +28.9). Follow-up unchanged: VST-17 (PLAY's pos readout and playhead redraw every 16th).
_screen_updates_per_s: offline proxy for ui_thread_pct (tests/test_plugin.c): measured about 1.2 ms of MPC_Main_Thread per update on the Force, so 60/s is about 7%. 2026-10-20, 0.20 (owner approved): 60 -> 65 for the MELODY JAM page: the BASS RHYTHM page measured 61.7/s at 160 BPM FOLLOW on (58.2 in 0.19.1; the JAM page's KEYS follow the playing bar, +4.9/s, and its phrase bars light, +1.4/s, on every page, while the retired MELODY FIX cells save 2.8/s); the real UI-thread cost is to be measured on the Force. 2026-10-20, 0.20 (owner approved): 65 -> 80 for the PHRASE page's live dots: PHRASE measured 68.3/s (INIT, 10 s) and 77.4/s (Canon 8 chords, 30 s) at 160 BPM FOLLOW on; the DOTS probe showed the device cost is mostly per redraw, not per dot; real UI-thread cost to be measured on the Force
_web: The browser version's speed, checked by tests/web_page.mjs --perf (run by tests/web_tests.sh alone, after the parity runs) in headless Chromium: medians of repeated trials, the worst printed beside them. 2026-10-29 (owner asked for a latency guardrail; measured then in Chrome on the owner's Mac: Play to sound 2-8 ms, tap to screen 26-30 ms, screen after sound 5 ms, 0.01-0.04 ms a frame). Sources for the limits: musicians stop noticing a delay below about 10 ms and lose tempo past about 20-30 ms (research on networked performance), Google's INP calls 200 ms or less 'good' and RAIL aims at 100 ms for a response, and a frame at 60 fps has 16.7 ms. Play to sound and screen after sound: 50 ms (the device's own output latency, about 15-35 ms, comes on top and is only reported). Tap to screen: 100 ms. The page's work per frame: 4 ms, a quarter of a frame. Raise only with the owner, as for the Force's budget.
